## 固定收益開盤主論

8月25日油價跌幅明顯擴大，延續前一交易日的通膨紓壓效果，並使政策敏感天期更充分參與行情，美債殖利率因而全線下滑。2年期殖利率下降5.9個基點至4.175%，5年期下降6.6個基點至4.336%，10年期下降6.8個基點至4.63%，30年期則下降6.1個基點至5.166%。

這是一波廣泛的漲勢，並非長端干預交易再度升溫。2s10s曲線趨平0.9個基點至45.5個基點，2s30s則幾乎不變，報99.1個基點。10年期實質殖利率下降5.2個基點至2.316%，10年期損益兩平通膨率也下降1.6個基點至2.314%。實質殖利率下降仍是名目利率走低的主要動力，但通膨補償同步下滑，顯示能源價格變動也開始影響市場對中期物價的看法。

布蘭特原油期貨下跌6.69%至$86，WTI下跌4.65%至$81.06。伊朗與阿曼正討論旨在恢復荷莫茲海峽航運的臨時框架；另有報導指出，美國正準備讓外交人員返回中東地區使館，也降低了市場對全面衝突即將重啟的擔憂。恢復能源運輸仍停留在討論階段，航道尚未重新開放，但原油跌勢之大，使美債獲得比週一較小跌幅更直接的通膨降溫動力。

與此同時，美國數據呈現預期轉弱、當前需求部分指標仍有韌性的分化格局。消費者信心降至7個月低點，企業景氣與就業前景惡化，但對當前情勢的評估改善。ADP每週就業成長與零售銷售指標較強；房市方面，房價年增率走高，月度活動則持平。這組數據有利殖利率下降，卻不足以判定國內需求是否正迅速降溫，進而讓聯準會得以維持利率不變。

兩位聯準會官員的談話也保留了政策的條件性。今年沒有投票權的波士頓聯準銀行總裁Susan Collins支持維持利率不變，但她表示，只有通膨持續降溫才能延續這項立場；若進展停滯，近期收緊政策將屬適當。今年同樣沒有投票權的里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin則稱7月決策相當接近，並認為在9月15日至16日會議前還有更多數據可供參考，因此值得等待。

財政部長Scott Bessent宣布的回購計畫繼續影響長端：美債表現優於相同天期的利率交換，選擇權部位也轉趨看多。不過，Bessent昔日導師Stanley Druckenmiller罕見地提出直接反對，認為官方壓低長期殖利率並不能解決背後的財政問題。黃金期貨上漲1.58%至$4,714，美元指數小跌0.09%，反映美債殖利率下降之際，市場仍有對沖財政與匯率風險的需求。

風險資產也受惠於壓力緩解。Nvidia公布財報前，標普500指數上漲0.32%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.64%，費城半導體指數上漲1.44%。投資級與高收益債券基金同步上漲，新興市場債則上升0.56%。因此，本日最重要的變化是能源成本下降帶動融資條件普遍放鬆；但美國通膨、債務管理，以及AI投資週期需要投入多少資本，仍是未解問題。

## 油價緩解壓力，美債漲勢擴至全曲線

原油下跌改變了美債行情的規模與組成。週一市場考量財政部是否可能運用現金餘額擴大回購，漲勢偏向較長天期。到了週二，2年期也加入上漲行列，2年、5年、10年與30年期殖利率的跌幅彼此相差不到1個基點。這波近乎平行的變動，使主要殖利率曲線斜率大致不變，未延續先前的趨平走勢。

布蘭特原油跌破$90是核心因素。伊朗與阿曼表示，雙方正討論恢復荷莫茲海峽航運的臨時框架；美國外交人員可能返回區域使館，也被解讀為華府並不預期局勢立即升高。布蘭特油價仍高於衝突前水準，因此戰爭造成的能源溢價並未消失，但近期壓抑主權債表現的通膨壓力已有相當部分反轉。

實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率的變化凸顯了這項差別。10年期實質殖利率下降5.2個基點，解釋了名目殖利率6.8個基點跌幅中的大部分；損益兩平通膨率下降1.6個基點，幅度雖較小，卻已不可忽略。損益兩平通膨率報2.314%，幾乎等同2.316%的實質殖利率，但兩者只是名目利率中的不同構成項目恰好處於相近水準，並非共同的經濟門檻。

較長天期資產的報酬同時反映債市上漲及其較高的利率敏感度。20年以上到期美債指數上漲1.09%，高於7至10年期的0.55%與1至3年期的0.11%。長天期高評級公司債指數上漲約1.0%至1.1%，顯示即使缺少涵蓋全市場的當日利差數據，政府債殖利率曲線下降仍明顯提振利率敏感度較高的信用債。

交易活動相當活躍。FINRA記錄的美債面額交易量為$1.216兆，較前一交易日增加13.3%；名目附息債交易量則增加15.3%至$1.005兆。增量主要不在超長端：2年內到期附息債的成交額激增72.3%至$2,681億，超過5年至7年期區間的成交額增加44.7%至$816億；20年以上區間則下降23.7%至$821億。

這些數字無法判斷客戶是淨買方或淨賣方，卻顯示美債普漲之際，短、中天期附息債的交易顯著增加。因此，2年期殖利率參與下跌並非長債行情在數學上的連帶結果；投資人也在重新評估油價下跌與當日經濟數據對通膨及政策的影響。

跨資產反應也符合即期能源衝擊緩解的情境。股市上漲，VIX下降2.52%至15.45，美元小幅走弱。黃金與債券同向上漲，並未只是扮演單純的通膨避險工具：期貨升至$4,714，單週漲幅接近8%。實質殖利率下降支撐金價，而市場對財政政策及官方干預債市的疑慮，繼續維持對主權債體系以外資產的需求。

不過，油價情勢仍有前提。荷莫茲海峽航運談判並不代表船運、保險供給或運費已恢復正常。美國也威脅對繼續與伊朗交易的國家施加經濟處罰；中國約購買伊朗90%的石油，因此尤其容易受到影響。即使近期軍事風險繼續下降，若制裁執法嚴厲到足以壓縮實體供給，週二油價帶來的部分通膨降溫效果仍可能逆轉。

## 聯準會耐心有條件，美國數據強弱不一

美國消費者信心是國內成長最明確的警訊。經濟評議會8月指數下降0.8點至89.4，前月數據也遭下修，創7個月最低。未來6個月預期指標降至1月以來低點，當前情勢指標則升至4個月高點。

這項分歧顯示民眾轉趨謹慎，卻尚未證明當前活動已經收縮。家庭對未來企業景氣、就業與所得的擔憂加深，但對當前情勢的評價有所改善。週二油價大跌前的高汽油價格、整體生活成本及招聘放緩都壓抑信心。相較信心指數本身，這種謹慎是否進一步轉化為消費走弱，對政策路徑更為重要。

同日其他指標仍然好壞互見。ADP每週就業成長由9.5K增至11.75K，這項數據沒有顯示就業突然惡化。截至8月22日當週，Redbook同店銷售年增率由7.6%加速至9.1%，表示儘管信心走弱，名目零售成長仍有韌性。

7月建築許可終值按年率計為143.3萬戶，高於前值137.4萬戶，但低於市場共識的144.3萬戶。月增率為4.3%，扭轉前月下降2.6%的走勢，卻不及預期的5%。這顯示住宅建築意向已由前月回升，但未超過市場修正後的預期。

房價數據也呈現類似分化。6月標普CoreLogic Case-Shiller房價指標年增2.1%，高於前值1.6%與市場共識1.7%。另一項房價指數由442.4微升至442.5，幾乎沒有變化；月增率為0%，低於0.2%的市場共識及前月0.3%的增幅，年增率則由修正後的2.4%放緩至2.3%。

綜合而言，這些數據並未顯示需求全面流失。信心與房價月度動能轉弱，但零售銷售成長、每週就業及房價年增率仍具韌性。這種組合說明了美債漲勢何以能延伸至前端，卻未能證明聯準會的通膨爭論已告結束。

Collins清楚說明了她保持耐心的條件。她支持7月維持利率不變，並認為近期溫和的基礎通膨數據略具鼓舞性，但提醒月度數據可能波動。依她的看法，只有通膨持續朝2%前進，才足以維持目前的聯邦基金利率區間；若無法確認進展持續，近期收緊政策便屬適當。

她的評估保留了展望的正反兩面。具限制性的短期利率與較高的長期殖利率，應能抑制家庭及企業強勁支出所產生的通膨壓力。Collins也預期，先前關稅轉嫁大多已經發生，油價上漲對通膨的影響將逐漸消退；週二能源價格下跌符合這條較溫和的路徑。

不過，她仍將負面供給衝擊與經濟活動強於預期列為可能的通膨上行風險。她表示，AI建設似乎正在推升核心商品通膨。這使聯準會的政策爭論不只涉及資料中心債券供給：即使市場期待的生產力提升尚未擴大經濟產能，這波投資熱潮已能支撐設備與原物料需求。

Barkin主張等待的理由較偏向決策程序，但條件性並未較低。他說7月維持利率不變是一項相當接近的決定，並重申通膨下降支持目前按兵不動，但也承認根深蒂固的物價壓力可能需要升息。7月至9月會議之間，官員將取得額外2個月的經濟資料；Barkin表示，截至週二已看到其中一套完整數據，現正等待下一套。

因此，兩位地區聯準銀行總裁都沒有暗示將無條件維持利率不變。Collins把立場直接繫於通膨能否持續改善；Barkin則強調行動前再觀察一輪數據的價值。兩人今年都沒有投票權，但其談話顯示，2年期殖利率下降5.9個基點應解讀為近期緊縮壓力減輕，而不是升息辯論已經確定結束。

## 回購支撐面臨財政可信度考驗

Bessent擴大回購的計畫已產生可觀察的市場效果，但外界對其目的與持久性的批評也在增加。自宣布以來，美債表現優於相同天期的利率交換，30年期美債與交換利率之間的差距縮至2月以來最小。10年期交換利差也壓縮約3個基點，差距目前接近38個基點。

這種相對表現比殖利率普遍下降更能指向特定原因。美債殖利率與交換利率同步走低，可能反映成長、通膨或聯準會政策預期的改變；美債表現優於交換，則更直接指向市場預期政府債券將被收回、其稀缺價值改變，或回購日後可能再度擴大。

選擇權部位也呈現相關的不對稱。長債期貨買權相對賣權的需求增強，較短天期期貨的偏斜則更接近中性。2026年9月與12月合約中，未平倉量最高的4個履約價裡，買權未平倉量超過賣權的兩倍。這顯示市場更擔心干預可能迫使長期利率急跌，儘管結構性投資人仍在爭論，以財政前景衡量，目前殖利率是否依然過低。

市場因此形成官方提供有限度托底的觀感。花旗利率策略師Jason Williams表示，這項公告使持有長端的風險報酬更偏向有利一側，因為投資人現在有理由預期，若殖利率突然上升，財政部可能出手。這種預期無須建立在政府能控制均衡利率的假設上，仍可改變空頭部位，以及投資人為承擔近期尾端風險所要求的價格。

Druckenmiller的反對意見，正是針對戰術性影響與經濟基本面之間的差別。這位Bessent昔日導師認為，政府應讓長期殖利率傳遞財政政策訊息，而不是捍衛偏好的價格。他以市場運作有序為由，不接受財政部所稱的流動性理由，並表示10年期殖利率大致等同經濟名目成長率，並不代表金融條件異常緊縮。

這項批評格外受到重視，因為Druckenmiller與Bessent過去曾共同從事以政府及央行終究無法無限抵抗市場壓力為基礎的交易。他認為，回購可以暫時壓抑財政訊號，卻不會改變支出、債務發行或通膨。若以增加短期借款為回購融資，也可能把壓力轉移至殖利率曲線其他區段或美元。

在目前財政環境下，這項質疑很難與債務管理分開看待。聯邦債務已超過$40兆；國會審議中的方案，包括主要與伊朗戰爭相關的本年度額外$950億支出，以及再增加$3,500億國防支出的提案。10月1日新會計年度即將開始，國會也預計把現有機關預算延長至12月中旬。

Bessent表示，即將提出的財政整頓方案將納入減少詐欺，但目前報導並未提供可量化的赤字效果。過去透過行政效率大幅節省開支的努力未達目標；數千億美元的削減提案一旦遭遇選情激烈選區的反對，國會議員也曾退縮。距國會選舉僅略多於2個月，政治時程進一步壓縮了近期採取不受歡迎措施的空間。

國際貨幣基金也強調了更廣泛的疑慮。總裁Kristalina Georgieva敦促各國政府提出可信計畫，使債務與赤字走上可持續路徑，並呼籲央行繼續專注於物價穩定。她形容全球經濟夾在中東造成的負面供給衝擊與AI投資形成的正面需求衝擊之間；高債券殖利率與尚未完成的通膨降溫，正凸顯其中壓力。

Barkin也直接談到債務風險。他表示，只要投資人仍願意購買美國證券，美國就能持續舉債，美元的全球地位與法治提供了支撐；但他警告，債務持續增加終將付出代價，只是何時發生無從判斷。他並不是指當前已出現融資失靈，而是指出投資人最終可能要求截然不同融資條件的風險。

因此，週二行情強化了回購確實能在邊際影響市場的證據，卻未回答回購能否持續降低借款成本。油價下跌、預期指標轉弱與空頭回補，都各自為美債提供支撐。交換利差收窄及長債選擇權轉趨看多，反映干預效果，但無法證明造成殖利率偏高的財政供給已經減少。

## AI融資拓展至新市場與私募架構

AI融資週期不僅改變借款人選擇的發行地點，也改變投資人評估信用風險的方式。韓國輸出入銀行週二在紐西蘭發行NZ$6.25億、5年期債券，約合$3.72億。這是該行約9年來首次進入Kauri債券市場，也是韓國發行人在當地規模最大的一筆交易。這家AA評級政策性銀行原先設定的最低發行額為NZ$2.5億，之後予以擴大。

韓國輸出入銀行明確表示，選擇這項幣別是因美國與歐洲初級市場過度擁擠；超大型雲端服務商大量舉債，已推升其他借款人的發行成本。紐西蘭市場2026年債券發行額約NZ$185億，甚至低於部分單一全球科技融資案的規模。當地AI相關債務較少，讓韓國輸出入銀行得以接觸受該產業供給影響較小的投資人。

這筆交易說明，AI借款造成的壓力不一定只以科技發行人利差擴大的形式出現。只要避險後的經濟效益仍然可行，高評級借款人可以更換幣別、市場與投資人基礎。今年韓國輸出入銀行也曾以美元、歐元、澳幣、港幣、英鎊及其他幣別發債，因此比規模較小或評級較低的借款人更有能力轉移融資來源。

市場對下一階段的擔憂不只在於公開債券的供給量。Sycamore Tree Capital Partners共同創辦人Trey Parker表示，資料中心需要數兆美元資金，將帶來施工、到期時點及保險公司採用的私募評級等風險。產業對私募信貸的需求可以支撐發行，但若監管機關質疑評級認定，或要求低估風險的資產配置更多資本，保險公司也會面臨曝險。

美國全國保險監理官協會正檢視私募信貸評級架構是否充分反映各評級提供者之間的差異。評級會決定保險公司必須持有多少監管資本，因此這項檢視相當重要。即使基礎貸款尚未違約，後續降評或監管待遇改變仍可能迫使保險公司出售資產，或減少法定盈餘。

Parker把目前的發展順序與世紀之交的電信熱潮相比；當時融資能力先成熟，需求與定價卻尚未獲得證明。他並未直接把目前市場稱為信用泡沫，而是聚焦到期時點與開發風險。Morgan Stanley與Moody’s估計未來幾年AI資本支出將達$3兆以上，JPMorgan若計入相關電力基礎設施，則預估支出超過$5兆。

今年AI相關債務發行額已超過$4,000億。部分投資級專案必須吸引高收益債投資人參與，承銷商也開始把交易間隔拉長；需求降溫時，發行人會釋出放慢交易步調的訊號。融資市場並未關閉，但投資人日益重視承租人信用、攤還安排、完工風險，以及資金必須償還的時間點。

當貸方、借款人與資產所有人互為關係企業時，私募信貸架構也會增加治理風險。Delaware Life先前申報約3%的投資資產涉及關係企業，之後重列為超過40%，約$160億。Fitch表示，修正後該公司在其評等的美國壽險業者中，關係企業投資曝險最高。

Mark Walter在不到一年前以$100億估值買下洛杉磯湖人隊控制權，如今已同意以據報$125億的估值，把球隊出售給Josh Kushner與Bob Iger。這筆出售可能為Walter控制的保險公司相關義務提供流動性；這些保險公司曾為洛杉磯道奇隊及相關實體融資。TWG Global也宣布，計畫向Delaware Life收購最多$65億資產。

將稀缺的運動球隊變現，或許有助於穩定這些特定資產負債表，但不能代表多數私募信貸抵押品。中型市場軟體公司或不動產專案可能與其贊助方同步轉弱，也未必具有透明或持續升值的市場價值。高度集中的關係企業曝險屆時可能使信用損失演變為監管資本問題；若多家保險公司同時受影響，還可能引發被迫賣出。

企業重整同樣凸顯受償順位與控制權的重要性。Braskem取得代表約39%債權的債權人支持後，針對約$110億債務啟動為期90天的庭外程序。這已跨過啟動程序所需的三分之一門檻，但股東支援、延長到期日及新增流動性的受償順位仍未達成共識。

Petrobras把Braskem採購原料的信用額度提高23.5億雷亞爾，約合$4.56億。債權人要求任何股東提供的流動性都必須劣後於其債權，但提案內容只表示簽署協議的債權人預期會採取此種順位安排。他們也反對把到期日延後5年並包含2.5年寬限期的提議。Petrobras持有約47%的表決權資本，卻未承諾提供債權人所要求的直接股權注資，部分原因是併表Braskem可能引發政治與立法上的複雜問題。

Aston Martin債權人則針對一筆涉及BlackRock旗下HPS及Authentic Brands英國子公司的£4.5億融資案，另闢法律戰線；該案約合$6.13億。Arini Capital Management與Tresidor Investment Management要求美國法院授權向HPS、Authentic Brands、Moelis及Lazard發出傳票，以取得文件與證詞，供預計在英國提出的訴訟使用。債券持有人主張，這筆交易繞過現有債權人；Aston Martin律師則表示，交易符合適用法律與債券文件。

在這些案例中，決定信用結果的是融資條款，而非整體市場上漲。公開債券市場仍然開放，美債殖利率下降也改善了當日報酬，但更棘手的問題是由哪個實體提供支援、新資金屬優先或次順位、評級如何轉化為保險公司的資本要求，以及債權人能否取得執行現有保障所需的資訊。

## 全球政策與主權信用走勢分歧

匈牙利完成了市場在週二決策前已經預期的寬鬆措施。匈牙利國家銀行把基準利率調降25個基點至5.5%，為連續第三次降息，也符合受訪20位經濟學家的一致預測。總裁Mihaly Varga表示，後續路徑將在9月會議決定，屆時決策者會取得更新後的通膨預測。

總理Peter Magyar領導的政府正推動採用歐元，最終將適用2%的通膨目標；央行也因此檢討目前3%的目標，並將於秋季公布結果。7月整體通膨降至1.2%，為2016年以來最低。央行6月預測2026年平均通膨為1.8%，低於3月預估的3.8%。

福林升值降低進口成本，帶來助益；但受財政與能源環境制約，不能據此一路外推降息步調。即使自首次降息以來福林已有回落，今年迄今仍升值逾6%。政府以先前支出及異常乾旱的成本為由，把預算赤字目標設為GDP的7.5%；能源價格偏高也仍可能改變9月的通膨展望。

日本的貨幣政策方向恰好相反。日本央行一項新的基礎通膨指標，以2025年為基期計算，7月年增2.3%。這項指標剔除生鮮食品及包括補貼效應在內的特定政府措施，仍高於日本央行2%的目標；政府傳統核心指標的增幅則為1.8%。

這項結果強化市場對日本央行9月18日會議升息的預期，交易員賦予的機率約為80%。經濟學家也把2027年前3個月的核心通膨預測由前次調查的2.8%上調至3%；政策預測中位數則顯示，基準利率將在2027年第3季達到1.75%。

緊縮展望已開始影響日本的預算計算。財務省計畫在明年4月開始的會計年度提出創紀錄的¥36.6兆債務服務預算要求，比本年度初始預算的¥31.28兆高17%。其中約¥16.6兆用於利息，¥20兆用於償還本金。官員採用3.8%的暫定利率，為近30年最高。

整體預算要求預計首次超過¥130兆。首相高市早苗的成長計畫與規劃中的消費稅減稅，尚未提出完整融資細節；各部會也正把經常性支出移入初始預算，降低對追加預算的依賴。即使最終發債計畫尚未出爐，這項債務服務預算要求已使JGB殖利率上升的財政成本更加明確。

印度則顯示定向外幣資金流入可以支撐國內殖利率曲線。自7月以來，HSBC已買進至少$30億印度政府債券，部位集中在5年期附近。截至7月30日，該行透過印度儲備銀行的外幣非居民特別存款計畫籌得$63億；知情人士表示，之後總額已超過$100億。

RBI計畫允許銀行以優惠條件把存款美元交換為盧比，排除匯率風險，並讓銀行取得可供投資的本地資金。各銀行透過這項僑民計畫合計吸收$654億，銀行體系剩餘流動性則升至約4兆盧比，為4月以來最高。自6月5日公布這項機制以來，5年期政府債殖利率已下降約31個基點，10年期則下降12個基點。

流動性也在支撐民間發債。Cholamandalam Investment and Finance計畫透過10年後可贖回的永續證券，籌資最多200億盧比，約合$2.09億。若交易完成，將成為印度民營非銀行機構規模最大的永續債發行，並追平國營REC在2023年發行的200億盧比。該公司6月止季度的放款年增22%，這筆資本將支援其繼續維持兩位數成長。

這項架構設有明確的損失吸收機制。印度非銀行發行人若資本水準低於監管最低標準，可以停止支付永續債本息；發生損失後償還債務也必須取得批准。這解釋了為何儘管整體流動性改善，非銀行永續債今年發行量仍銳減90%至46億盧比。

南非則顯示，即使沒有特殊存款機制，較高殖利率也能吸引需求。交易商對25.5億蘭特的固定利率政府債券提交147.9億蘭特訂單，投標倍數達5.8倍，高於一週前的4.6倍，並創6月2日以來最高。上週債市遭遇賣壓後，月底約490億蘭特的票息支付支撐再投資需求。

2037年債券發行額為8.5億蘭特，收到67.1億蘭特訂單，殖利率下降9個基點至8.75%。蘭特升值0.3%至每美元15.9844蘭特，收盤區域為6個月來最強。通膨趨緩、蘭特單月升值3.4%，以及市場預期10月預算將呈現較佳財政數據，都有助於支撐需求。

主權債的有利結果與約翰尼斯堡的市政壓力形成對比。發展與企業中心的研究發現，未繳帳款已由10年前的150億蘭特增至720億蘭特，約合$45億。員工相關支出每年成長逾9%至207億蘭特，每年基礎設施支出則由105億蘭特降至最低僅60億蘭特。

報告認為，收款不佳造成了自我強化循環：費率上升降低客戶付款的能力或意願，使市政府認列實際上並未收到的收入。約翰尼斯堡上週向Eskom支付52.6億蘭特的逾期電費，市長Dada Morero表示財務狀況正在改善。更廣泛的疑慮是，延遲支付Eskom及Rand Water，會把市政府的弱點轉移至其他公共實體。

墨西哥則呈現主權層級的資產負債表負擔轉移。現任及前任政府合計已向Pemex提供逾$1,300億支援，其中過去2年超過$500億。這些援助降低了公司的近期違約風險，但投資人與分析師表示，在財政赤字接近倍增之際，部分負擔已轉移給主權政府。

Pemex產量已降至每日170萬桶以下，約為20年前高峰的一半，債務仍超過$700億。Moody’s在5月把墨西哥評級調降至高於垃圾級一級，S&P則把評等展望列為負向。墨西哥美元債的殖利率過去比整體拉丁美洲市場低約1.5個百分點，如今優勢只剩略高於0.5個百分點。

政府計畫要求Pemex降低債務、提高產量，並在2027年前達成自給自足。公司表示，債務已較2018年高峰低近27%，現金流與利潤率也有所改善。分析師仍懷疑，如果不能降低勞動成本、投入新資本並引進更多鑽探專業，單靠減債能否恢復持久獲利能力。

綜觀這些市場，政策空間取決於通膨、匯率穩定與公共資產負債表的交互作用。物價成長放緩與福林強勢，讓匈牙利具有降息空間；日本則在為更高利率及更龐大的債務服務支出作準備。印度的存款計畫正壓低中期借款成本，南非債券則受惠於殖利率與再投資需求。約翰尼斯堡及墨西哥顯示，即使國家債券市場仍然開放，負債仍可能在公共部門內部轉移。

## 後市意義

8月26日公布的7月個人消費支出報告，是檢驗週二債市漲勢最近的一項指標。美債行情同時包含實質殖利率大幅下降與損益兩平通膨率較小幅度的下滑，當日經濟活動數據則是強弱不一，而非全面疲弱。若基礎通膨普遍溫和，將支持前端繼續參與漲勢；若服務或核心商品價格壓力再起，便會強化Collins所提的緊縮條件，使債市漲勢更加依賴油價下跌。

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh週五在Jackson Hole的演說，是影響政策反應函數的更重大事件。投資人希望他更清楚解釋聯準會7月為何維持利率不變、未來是否仍可能升息，以及他打算如何在減少前瞻指引之餘，繼續清楚傳達委員會的評估。7月記者會後30年期殖利率曾急升，因此解釋品質會同時影響政策預期與期限溢價。

財政部5年期及7年期債券標售，將測試殖利率下降、交易活動增加後，需求是否仍然穩健。回購計畫已改善美債相對交換利率的表現，也鼓勵建立長債看多部位；標售要回答的卻是另一個問題：市場須有何種價格條件，才能吸收持續進行的例行發行。需求強勁將鞏固債市漲勢；反應疲弱則會凸顯回購特定舊券與為整體赤字融資之間的差別。

荷莫茲海峽的後續發展仍是最直接的外部通膨風險。市場需要看到伊朗與阿曼的框架真正帶來航運恢復、保險成本下降及能源穩定流通。美國對伊朗石油買方施加的處罰可能產生反方向效果，特別是針對中國的措施若減少供給或引發報復。週二原油下跌反映局勢降溫預期，而不是衝突已經解決。

加拿大採取對等關稅，另增一項貿易價格風險。渥太華表示，將把美國鋼鋁關稅提高一倍至50%，並對牛奶、家具、服裝、智慧型手機及電玩遊戲機等商品課徵50%關稅。措施涵蓋逾700種產品及每年約$200億的美國出口，約占總額6%。這些措施對價格、生產及跨境需求的影響，將納入下一輪評估，以判斷關稅不確定性是否正在擴大。

韓國央行週四的決策是一場意見接近對半的政策考驗。22位經濟學家中有14位預期連續第二次升息25個基點至3%，另有8位預期維持不變。成長較強、通膨持續及房市槓桿支持升息；韓元升至約每美元1,383韓元，則降低輸入性物價壓力。相較利率決定本身，更新後的成長與通膨預測、6個月點陣圖，以及是否出現異議更值得關注。

日本9月18日會議將檢驗新的2.3%基礎通膨指標，是否足以把市場約80%的升息定價轉化為實際行動。決策也會與創紀錄的¥36.6兆債務服務預算要求一併評估。若政策正常化速度加快，將同時影響日本國內預算成本及全球長天期主權債的定價。

Braskem的90天協商必須處理股東支援的金額與受償順位、延長到期日5年的提案，以及Petrobras扮演的角色。Aston Martin債權人正在取得文件，以便在英國發起訴訟；保險監管機關則檢視私募資產的評級待遇。這些案例都已顯示市場仍可取得流動性，尚未解決的問題是流動性不足時誰具有優先順位。

AI融資是一項持續的市場容量考驗，而不是單一日曆事件。Nvidia財報將影響市場對終端需求的預期，但債券投資人也必須評估，預計$3兆至逾$5兆的支出，能否在融資架構不逐漸弱化的情況下獲得資金。韓國輸出入銀行發行Kauri債券一類的幣別多元化，可以在邊際緩解市場擁擠，卻無法取代清楚的承租人信用、具實質意義的攤還安排，以及在監管檢視下仍站得住腳的評級。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied across the curve on Aug. 25 as a much larger decline in oil extended the previous session’s inflation relief and brought policy-sensitive maturities more fully into the move. The 2-year yield fell 5.9 basis points to 4.175%, the 5-year dropped 6.6 basis points to 4.336%, the 10-year declined 6.8 basis points to 4.63% and the 30-year fell 6.1 basis points to 5.166%.

The rally was broad rather than a renewed long-end intervention trade. The 2s10s curve flattened 0.9 basis point to 45.5 basis points, while 2s30s was almost unchanged at 99.1 basis points. The 10-year real yield fell 5.2 basis points to 2.316%, and the 10-year breakeven declined 1.6 basis points to 2.314%. Lower required real yields still did most of the work, but the fall in inflation compensation showed that the energy move was also beginning to affect the market’s medium-term price outlook.

Brent futures lost 6.69% to $86 and WTI fell 4.65% to $81.06. Iran and Oman were discussing an interim framework intended to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while a report that the US was preparing to return diplomats to Middle East embassies reduced concern about an imminent renewal of full-scale conflict. The prospective improvement in energy flows was not yet a completed reopening, but the scale of the crude decline gave Treasuries a more direct disinflationary impulse than Monday’s smaller move.

The rally also occurred as US data separated weaker expectations from firmer elements of current demand. Consumer confidence slipped to a 7-month low, with the outlook for business conditions and employment deteriorating even as an assessment of present conditions improved. Weekly ADP employment growth and retail-sales indicators were firmer, while housing data showed stronger annual prices alongside flat monthly activity. The combination supported lower yields without settling whether domestic demand is cooling quickly enough to keep the Federal Reserve on hold.

Two Fed officials preserved that conditionality. Boston Fed President Susan Collins, a nonvoter, supported leaving rates unchanged but said continued evidence of disinflation was necessary to maintain that stance and that tightening soon would be appropriate if progress stalled. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin, also a nonvoter, called July’s decision a close call and said the additional data available before the Sept. 15-16 meeting justified waiting.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s buyback announcement continued to influence the long end, where Treasuries have outperformed comparable swaps and options positioning has become more bullish. Yet the session also brought unusually direct objections from Stanley Druckenmiller, Bessent’s former mentor, who argued that official attempts to suppress long yields would not resolve the fiscal conditions behind them. Gold futures rose 1.58% to $4,714 and the Dollar Index edged 0.09% lower, showing that lower Treasury yields coexisted with continued demand for protection against fiscal and currency risk.

Risk assets participated in the relief. The S&P 500 rose 0.32%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.64% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index advanced 1.44% ahead of Nvidia’s results. Investment-grade and high-yield bond funds also gained, while emerging-market debt rose 0.56%. The day’s defining change was therefore a broad easing in financing conditions led by cheaper energy, tempered by unresolved questions about US inflation, debt management and the volume of capital required by the AI investment cycle.

## Oil Relief Broadens the Treasury Rally

The fall in crude changed both the size and composition of the Treasury move. Monday’s rally had favored longer maturities as investors considered whether Treasury might use its cash balance to support expanded repurchases. On Tuesday, the 2-year joined the advance, and the declines in 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields were clustered within less than 1 basis point of one another. The almost parallel move left the principal curve slopes little changed rather than extending the earlier flattening.

Brent’s decline below $90 was central. Iran and Oman said they were discussing an interim framework aimed at resuming shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and the prospect of US diplomats returning to regional embassies was interpreted as evidence that Washington did not expect immediate escalation. Brent remained above levels prevailing before the conflict, so the move did not remove the war-related energy premium. It did reverse a meaningful part of the inflation pressure that had recently weighed on sovereign bonds.

That distinction appeared in the split between real yields and breakevens. The 5.2-basis-point decline in the 10-year real yield accounted for most of the 6.8-basis-point nominal move, while the 1.6-basis-point fall in the breakeven showed a smaller but no longer negligible reduction in inflation compensation. The resulting 2.314% breakeven was nearly identical to the 2.316% real yield, but the matching levels reflected separate components of the nominal rate rather than a common economic threshold.

Long-duration returns reflected both the rally and their greater interest-rate sensitivity. An index of Treasuries maturing in more than 20 years gained 1.09%, compared with 0.55% for the 7- to 10-year sector and 0.11% for 1- to 3-year debt. Long-dated high-grade corporate indexes rose by roughly 1.0% to 1.1%, showing how the lower government curve lifted duration-heavy credit even without a broad same-day spread measure.

Trading activity was substantial. FINRA recorded $1.216 trillion of Treasury par activity, 13.3% more than the previous session, while nominal-coupon activity rose 15.3% to $1.005 trillion. The increase was concentrated away from the very long end: turnover in coupons maturing within 2 years surged 72.3% to $268.1 billion, and activity in the greater-than-5-year through 7-year sector climbed 44.7% to $81.6 billion. Activity beyond 20 years fell 23.7% to $82.1 billion.

Those figures do not identify whether customers were net buyers or sellers, but they show that the broad rally was accompanied by a marked increase in transactions in short and intermediate coupons. The participation of the 2-year yield therefore was not merely an arithmetic consequence of a long-bond move. Investors were also reassessing the inflation and policy implications of the oil decline and the day’s economic releases.

The cross-asset response was consistent with relief from an immediate energy shock. Equities rose, the VIX declined 2.52% to 15.45 and the dollar weakened slightly. Gold moved in the same direction as bonds rather than behaving as a simple inflation hedge: futures gained to $4,714 and were almost 8% higher over one week. Lower real yields supported the metal, while concern about fiscal policy and official intervention in bond markets preserved demand for an asset outside the sovereign-debt system.

The oil story remained conditional. Discussions over Hormuz shipping did not establish that traffic, insurance availability or freight costs had normalized. The US was also threatening economic penalties against countries that continue trading with Iran, with China particularly exposed because it buys about 90% of Iranian oil. Enforcement severe enough to reduce physical supply could reverse part of Tuesday’s disinflationary move even if the immediate military risk continues to recede.

## Conditional Fed Patience Meets Uneven US Data

US consumer confidence supplied the clearest domestic growth warning. The Conference Board’s index fell 0.8 point to 89.4 in August after the previous month was revised lower, its weakest reading in 7 months. Expectations for the next 6 months dropped to the lowest level since January, while the present-conditions measure rose to a 4-month high.

The divergence matters because it describes caution before it establishes a contraction in current activity. Households were becoming more concerned about future business conditions, employment and income, but their assessment of the present had improved. High gasoline prices before Tuesday’s sharp decline, broader living costs and slower hiring were weighing on sentiment. Whether that caution turns into weaker spending remains more important for the policy path than the confidence index alone.

Other same-day indicators were mixed. Weekly ADP employment growth increased to 11.75K from 9.5K, providing no sign of an abrupt deterioration in that measure. Redbook same-store sales rose 9.1% from a year earlier in the week through Aug. 22, accelerating from 7.6%, which pointed to continued nominal retail strength despite weaker sentiment.

July building permits were finalized at an annualized 1.433 million, up from 1.374 million but below the 1.443 million consensus. The monthly increase was 4.3%, reversing a 2.6% decline but falling short of the expected 5%. The figures showed residential construction intentions recovering from the prior month without exceeding the market’s revised expectation.

House-price releases presented a similarly divided picture. The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller measure rose 2.1% from a year earlier in June, accelerating from 1.6% and exceeding the 1.7% consensus. The separate house-price index was nearly unchanged at 442.5 versus 442.4 previously. Its monthly change was 0%, below the 0.2% consensus and the previous 0.3% increase, while annual growth slowed to 2.3% from a revised 2.4%.

Taken together, the releases did not describe a uniform loss of demand. Confidence and monthly house-price momentum weakened, but retail sales growth, weekly employment and annual home-price appreciation retained firmness. That mix helps explain why the Treasury rally reached the front end without producing evidence that the Fed’s inflation debate had been resolved.

Collins made the conditions for her patience explicit. She supported the July hold and described recent subdued underlying inflation readings as mildly encouraging, but warned that monthly data can be volatile. Maintaining the current federal-funds range, in her view, requires continued evidence that inflation is moving toward 2%; failure to establish sustained progress would make near-term tightening appropriate.

Her assessment preserved both sides of the outlook. Restrictive short-term rates and higher long-term yields should restrain inflationary pressure from strong household and business spending. Collins also expects most of the earlier tariff pass-through to have occurred and the inflation effect of higher oil prices to wane. Tuesday’s energy decline was consistent with that more benign path.

She nevertheless identified adverse supply shocks and stronger-than-expected activity as plausible upside risks. The AI buildout, she said, appeared to be placing upward pressure on core-goods inflation. That observation ties the Fed debate to more than data-center bond supply: the investment boom can support demand for equipment and materials even before its hoped-for productivity gains expand economic capacity.

Barkin’s argument for waiting was more procedural but no less conditional. He said the July hold was a close call and repeated that declining inflation supported steady rates for now, while acknowledging that embedded price pressure could require an increase. Officials will receive 2 additional months of economic information between the July and September meetings; by Tuesday, Barkin said, they had seen one full set and were waiting for another.

The two regional presidents therefore did not signal an unconditional hold. Collins attached her stance directly to sustained inflation improvement. Barkin emphasized the value of another data cycle before acting. Neither votes this year, but their comments show why the 5.9-basis-point fall in the 2-year yield should be read as reduced immediate pressure rather than a settled end to the tightening debate.

## Buyback Support Faces a Fiscal Credibility Test

Bessent’s expanded buyback plan is producing observable market effects even as criticism of its purpose and durability grows. Since the announcement, Treasuries have outperformed equivalent-maturity interest-rate swaps, and the 30-year spread between the two has narrowed to its smallest since February. The 10-year swap spread has also compressed by about 3 basis points, leaving the gap near 38 basis points.

That relative performance is more specific than a general decline in yields. A fall in Treasury yields alongside swaps can reflect changes in growth, inflation or expected Fed policy. Treasuries outperforming swaps points more directly toward the expected removal of government securities from the market, a change in their scarcity value or anticipation that purchases could be expanded again.

Options positioning shows a related asymmetry. Demand for calls on long-bond futures has strengthened relative to puts, while shorter-maturity futures skews have remained closer to neutral. In the 4 most populated strikes across September and December 2026 contracts, call open interest was more than twice put open interest. The positioning indicates greater concern that intervention could force long rates sharply lower, even though structural investors continue to debate whether current yields remain too low for the fiscal outlook.

The resulting market perception resembles a limited official backstop. Citigroup rates strategist Jason Williams described the announcement as improving the asymmetry of owning the long end because investors now have reason to expect Treasury to respond if yields rise abruptly. That expectation does not require the government to control the equilibrium rate. It can still alter short positioning and the price investors demand for near-term tail risk.

Druckenmiller’s objection targeted precisely that distinction between tactical influence and economic fundamentals. Bessent’s former mentor argued that the government should allow long-term yields to transmit information about fiscal policy instead of defending a preferred price. He rejected the Treasury’s liquidity rationale on the ground that the market was orderly and said the 10-year yield, at roughly the economy’s nominal growth rate, did not represent unusually restrictive financial conditions.

The criticism carries particular weight because Druckenmiller and Bessent previously worked together in trades built around the inability of governments and central banks to resist market pressure indefinitely. His argument was that buybacks could suppress the fiscal signal temporarily without changing spending, debt issuance or inflation. Financing purchases with more short-term borrowing could also transfer pressure elsewhere on the curve or into the dollar.

The current fiscal setting makes that objection difficult to separate from debt management. Federal debt has exceeded $40 trillion, and plans before Congress include $95 billion of additional current-year spending associated largely with the Iran war and proposals for another $350 billion of defense outlays. Congress is also approaching the Oct. 1 start of the fiscal year and is expected to extend existing agency funding into mid-December.

Bessent has indicated that fraud reduction will feature in a forthcoming consolidation plan, but current reporting did not provide a quantified deficit effect. Earlier attempts to achieve large savings through administrative efficiency fell short, while lawmakers have retreated from hundreds of billions of dollars of proposed cuts when they encountered opposition from competitive districts. The political calendar, with congressional elections little more than 2 months away, further narrows the immediate room for unpopular measures.

The IMF reinforced the broader concern. Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva urged governments to present credible plans that put debt and deficits on sustainable paths and called on central banks to remain focused on price stability. She described the world economy as caught between the negative supply shock from the Middle East and the positive demand shock from AI investment, with high bond yields and incomplete disinflation exposing the strain.

Barkin also addressed the debt risk directly. He said the US can continue borrowing as long as investors remain willing to buy its securities, supported by the dollar’s global role and the rule of law, but warned that continued debt growth would eventually produce a reckoning whose timing cannot be known. His point did not identify a current funding failure; it located the risk in the possibility that investors ultimately demand materially different terms.

Tuesday’s rally therefore strengthened the evidence that buybacks matter at the margin without answering whether they can produce a sustained decline in borrowing costs. Cheaper oil, weaker expectations data and short covering all supported Treasuries independently. The narrower swap spreads and bullish long-bond options show an intervention effect, but they do not demonstrate that the fiscal supply behind elevated yields has diminished.

## AI Funding Expands Into New Markets and Private Structures

The AI financing cycle is changing where borrowers issue as well as how investors assess credit risk. The Export-Import Bank of Korea sold NZ$625 million, or $372 million, of 5-year notes in New Zealand on Tuesday, its first Kauri-market transaction in about 9 years and the largest sale there by a Korean issuer. The AA-rated policy bank increased the deal from an initial minimum of NZ$250 million.

Kexim explicitly linked the currency choice to crowded primary markets in the US and Europe, where hyperscaler borrowing has raised issuance costs for other borrowers. New Zealand had hosted about NZ$18.5 billion of bond sales in 2026, less than some individual global technology financings. Its relative lack of AI-related debt offered Kexim a buyer base less saturated by the sector’s supply.

The transaction shows that the pressure from AI borrowing need not appear only as wider spreads for technology issuers. A high-grade borrower can respond by changing currency, market and investor base, provided the economics remain workable after hedging. Kexim has also issued in US dollars, euros, Australian and Hong Kong dollars, sterling and other currencies this year, giving it more capacity to redirect funding than smaller or lower-rated borrowers possess.

Concerns about the next stage extend beyond public bond volume. Sycamore Tree Capital Partners co-founder Trey Parker said the trillions of dollars required for data centers create risks around construction, maturity timing and the private ratings used by insurance companies. The industry’s demand for private credit can support issuance, but it also leaves insurers exposed if regulators challenge rating designations or require more capital against assets whose risk was understated.

The National Association of Insurance Commissioners is examining whether the framework for private-credit ratings adequately captures differences among rating providers. That inquiry matters because a rating can determine the amount of regulatory capital an insurer must hold. A later downgrade or change in treatment could force sales or reduce statutory surplus even if the underlying loan has not yet defaulted.

Parker compared the development sequence with the telecom boom around the turn of the century, when financing capacity matured before demand and pricing were proven. He stopped short of calling the current market a credit bubble, focusing instead on the timing of maturities and development risk. Morgan Stanley and Moody’s estimate AI capital expenditure at $3 trillion or more in coming years, while JPMorgan projects spending above $5 trillion including associated power infrastructure.

More than $400 billion of AI-linked debt has already been sold this year. Some investment-grade projects have required participation from high-yield buyers, underwriters have begun spacing transactions more widely, and issuers are signaling slower deal pacing when demand cools. The result is not a closure of financing markets but growing discrimination over tenant quality, amortization, completion risk and the point at which capital must be repaid.

Private-credit structures add governance risk when lender, borrower and asset owner are affiliated. Delaware Life previously reported that roughly 3% of its invested assets involved affiliates, then restated the figure to more than 40%, or about $16 billion. Fitch said the correction gave the insurer the highest affiliated-investment exposure among US life insurers it rated.

Mark Walter has agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger at a reported $12.5 billion valuation after buying control less than a year earlier at a $10 billion valuation. The sale may help generate liquidity for obligations connected to Walter-controlled insurers, which had financed the Los Angeles Dodgers and related entities. TWG Global also announced plans to acquire as much as $6.5 billion of assets from Delaware Life.

The ability to monetize scarce sports franchises could help stabilize those particular balance sheets, but it is not representative of most private-credit collateral. A middle-market software company or real-estate project may weaken at the same time as its sponsor and may not have a transparent or appreciating market value. Concentrated affiliate exposure can then turn a credit loss into a regulatory-capital problem and, across multiple insurers, create forced selling.

Company restructurings showed the same importance of priority and control. Braskem began a 90-day out-of-court process covering about $11 billion of debt after securing support from creditors representing roughly 39% of claims. That cleared the one-third threshold required to start the proceeding, but it did not produce agreement on shareholder support, maturity extensions or the ranking of new liquidity.

Petrobras increased Braskem’s credit limit for raw-material purchases by 2.35 billion reais, or $456 million. Creditors want any shareholder liquidity to rank behind their claims, while the proposed plan says only that signatory creditors expect such subordination. They are also resisting a proposed 5-year maturity extension that includes a 2.5-year grace period. Petrobras, which owns about 47% of voting capital, has avoided committing to the direct equity injection creditors seek, partly because consolidation of Braskem could raise political and legislative complications.

Aston Martin creditors opened a separate legal front over a £450 million, or $613 million, financing involving BlackRock’s HPS and a UK unit of Authentic Brands. Arini Capital Management and Tresidor Investment Management asked a US court to authorize subpoenas for documents and testimony from HPS, Authentic Brands, Moelis and Lazard for use in a planned UK challenge. Bondholders contend that the transaction circumvented existing creditors, while Aston Martin’s counsel has said it complied with applicable law and bond documents.

These cases place the financing terms, rather than the broad market rally, at the center of credit outcomes. Public debt markets remain open, and lower Treasury yields improved daily returns. The harder questions concern which entity provides support, whether new money is senior or subordinated, how ratings translate into insurer capital and whether creditors can obtain the information needed to enforce existing protections.

## Global Policy and Sovereign Credit Diverge

Hungary completed the easing step that had been expected before Tuesday’s decision. The National Bank of Hungary cut its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, its third consecutive reduction and the unanimous forecast of 20 surveyed economists. Governor Mihaly Varga said the path from here would be decided at the September meeting, when policymakers receive updated inflation projections.

The central bank is also reviewing its 3% inflation target as Prime Minister Peter Magyar’s government pursues euro adoption, which would eventually place Hungary under a 2% objective. The review will be published in the autumn. Headline inflation slowed to 1.2% in July, its lowest since 2016, while the central bank’s June forecast put average 2026 inflation at 1.8%, down from a 3.8% projection in March.

Forint appreciation has helped by lowering import costs, but the fiscal and energy backdrop limits a simple extrapolation of the easing cycle. The currency remains more than 6% stronger this year even after weakening since the first cut. The government is targeting a budget deficit of 7.5% of gross domestic product, citing earlier spending and the cost of an exceptional drought, while elevated energy prices could still alter the September inflation outlook.

Japan faces the opposite monetary direction. A new Bank of Japan measure of underlying inflation rose 2.3% from a year earlier in July on a 2025-base basis. The gauge excludes fresh food and selected government measures, including subsidy effects, and remained above the BOJ’s 2% target. That compared with a 1.8% rise in the government’s conventional core measure.

The result strengthened expectations for a rate increase at the BOJ’s Sept. 18 meeting, for which traders assigned roughly an 80% probability. Economists also raised their forecast for core inflation in the first 3 months of 2027 to 3% from 2.8% in the previous survey. Their median policy projection placed the benchmark rate at 1.75% by Q3 2027.

The tightening outlook is already affecting Japan’s budget arithmetic. The Finance Ministry plans to request a record ¥36.6 trillion, or $230 billion, for debt service in the fiscal year beginning in April, 17% more than the ¥31.28 trillion in the current initial budget. About ¥16.6 trillion would cover interest and ¥20 trillion redemptions. Officials used a provisional interest rate of 3.8%, the highest in nearly 3 decades.

The overall budget request is expected to exceed ¥130 trillion for the first time. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s growth program and planned sales-tax cut have not yet been matched with detailed financing, while ministries are moving recurring spending into the initial budget rather than relying as heavily on supplements. The debt-service request makes the fiscal cost of higher JGB yields increasingly explicit even before the final issuance plan is known.

India illustrated how directed foreign-currency inflows can support a domestic curve. HSBC has bought at least $3 billion of Indian government bonds, concentrated around the 5-year maturity, since July. The bank had raised $6.3 billion by July 30 under the Reserve Bank of India’s special foreign-currency nonresident deposit program, and people familiar with the matter said its total later exceeded $10 billion.

The RBI program allows banks to swap deposit dollars into rupees on concessional terms, removing their currency risk and leaving them with local funds to invest. Banks collectively attracted $65.4 billion through the diaspora scheme, while surplus banking-system liquidity rose to about 4 trillion rupees, its highest since April. The 5-year government yield has fallen about 31 basis points since the facility was announced on June 5, compared with 12 basis points for the 10-year.

That liquidity is supporting private issuance as well. Cholamandalam Investment and Finance plans to raise as much as 20 billion rupees, or $209 million, through perpetual securities callable after 10 years. If completed, the transaction would be the largest private non-bank perpetual sale in India and would match the 20 billion rupees issued by state-run REC in 2023. The issuer’s loans grew 22% from a year earlier in the June quarter, and the capital would support continued double-digit expansion.

The structure carries explicit loss-absorption features. Indian non-bank issuers can stop servicing perpetual debt if capitalization falls below regulatory minimums and need approval to repay it after a loss. That helps explain why non-bank perpetual issuance has fallen 90% this year to 4.6 billion rupees despite the broader improvement in liquidity.

South Africa showed elevated yields attracting demand without a special deposit mechanism. Dealers placed 14.79 billion rand of orders for 2.55 billion rand of fixed-rate government bonds, producing a 5.8 bid-to-cover ratio, the highest since June 2 and up from 4.6 a week earlier. Month-end coupon payments of about 49 billion rand supported reinvestment demand after the previous week’s selloff.

The 2037 bond received 6.71 billion rand of orders for 850 million rand offered, and its yield fell 9 basis points to 8.75%. The rand strengthened 0.3% to 15.9844 per dollar, its strongest closing area in 6 months. Moderating inflation, a 3.4% monthly currency gain and expectations of better fiscal metrics in the October budget contributed to the demand.

That favorable sovereign result contrasted with municipal stress in Johannesburg. A study by the Centre for Development and Enterprise found that unpaid bills had risen to 72 billion rand, or $4.5 billion, from 15 billion rand a decade earlier. Employee-related expenses grew by more than 9% annually to 20.7 billion rand, while yearly infrastructure spending fell as low as 6 billion rand from 10.5 billion rand.

The report argued that weak collection had produced a self-reinforcing cycle in which higher tariffs reduced customers’ ability or willingness to pay, leaving the city to recognize revenue it did not receive. Johannesburg paid Eskom 5.26 billion rand in overdue electricity bills last week, and Mayor Dada Morero said finances were improving. The wider concern is that delayed payments to Eskom and Rand Water shift municipal weakness onto other public entities.

Mexico presents a sovereign version of balance-sheet transfer. The government has provided more than $130 billion of support to Pemex across the current and previous administrations, including more than $50 billion in the past 2 years. The assistance reduced immediate default risk at the company, but investors and analysts said it transferred part of the burden to the sovereign as the fiscal deficit nearly doubled.

Pemex’s production has fallen below 1.7 million barrels a day, about half its peak 2 decades ago, while debt remains above $70 billion. Moody’s cut Mexico to one notch above junk in May, and S&P placed a negative outlook on its rating. Mexican dollar bonds, which once yielded about 1.5 percentage points less than the wider Latin American market, now offer only a little more than a half-point advantage.

The government’s plan calls for Pemex to reduce debt, raise production and become self-sufficient by 2027. The company said debt was nearly 27% below its 2018 peak and that cash flow and margins had improved. Analysts remain skeptical that debt reduction alone can restore durable profitability without lower labor costs, new capital and additional drilling expertise.

Across these markets, policy latitude depends on the interaction between inflation, currency stability and public balance sheets. Hungary can cut because price growth and the forint created room. Japan is preparing for higher rates and a larger debt-service bill. India’s deposit program is anchoring intermediate borrowing costs, while South African bonds are benefiting from yield and reinvestment demand. Johannesburg and Mexico show how liabilities can migrate within the public sector even when the national bond market remains open.

## Forward Market Significance

The July personal-consumption-expenditure report on Aug. 26 is the nearest test of Tuesday’s rally. The Treasury move combined a substantial fall in real yields with a smaller decline in breakevens, while same-day activity data were mixed rather than uniformly weak. Broadly subdued underlying inflation would support the front end’s participation; renewed services or core-goods pressure would strengthen Collins’s condition for tightening and leave the rally more dependent on oil.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole address on Friday is the larger reaction-function event. Investors are seeking a clearer explanation of why the Fed held rates steady in July, whether increases remain available and how Warsh intends to reduce forward guidance without obscuring the committee’s assessment. The 30-year yield surged after his July press conference, making the quality of the explanation relevant to both expected policy and the term premium.

The Treasury’s 5- and 7-year auctions will test whether demand remains firm after yields fell and trading activity increased. The buyback plan has improved the relative performance of Treasuries against swaps and encouraged bullish long-bond positioning, but the auctions address a different question: the price required to absorb continuing regular issuance. Strong demand would reinforce the rally; a weak reception would expose the distinction between removing selected older bonds and financing the broader deficit.

Hormuz developments remain the most immediate external inflation risk. Markets will need evidence that the Iran-Oman framework produces actual shipping, lower insurance costs and sustained energy flows. US penalties aimed at buyers of Iranian oil could work in the opposite direction, particularly if measures against China reduce supply or provoke retaliation. Tuesday’s decline in crude reflected de-escalation expectations, not a completed settlement.

Canada’s matching tariffs add a separate trade-price risk. Ottawa said it would double duties on US steel and aluminum to 50% and apply 50% levies to products including milk, furniture, clothing, smartphones and video-game consoles. The measures cover more than 700 products and about $20 billion of annual US exports, roughly 6% of the total. Their effect on prices, production and cross-border demand will become part of the next assessment of whether tariff uncertainty is broadening.

The Bank of Korea’s Thursday decision presents a closely divided policy test. Fourteen of 22 economists expect a second consecutive 25-basis-point increase to 3%, while 8 expect a hold. Stronger growth, persistent inflation and housing leverage argue for tightening; the won’s rise to about 1,383 per dollar reduces imported-price pressure. Updated growth and inflation forecasts, the 6-month dot plot and any dissent will matter more than the rate decision alone.

Japan’s Sept. 18 meeting will test whether the new 2.3% underlying-inflation measure is enough to convert roughly 80% market pricing into another increase. The decision will also be judged against the record ¥36.6 trillion debt-service request. A faster normalization path would affect both domestic budget costs and the global price of long-duration sovereign debt.

Braskem’s 90-day negotiation must resolve the amount and seniority of shareholder support, the proposed 5-year maturity extension and Petrobras’s role. Aston Martin’s creditors are seeking documents before mounting their UK challenge, while insurer regulators are examining the rating treatment of private assets. In each case, access to liquidity is already visible; the unresolved issue is who ranks ahead when that liquidity is insufficient.

AI financing remains a continuing capacity test rather than a single calendar event. Nvidia’s results will shape expectations for end demand, but bond investors also need to assess whether projected spending of $3 trillion to more than $5 trillion can be funded without progressively weaker structures. Currency diversification such as Kexim’s Kauri sale can relieve crowded markets at the margin. It cannot remove the need for clear tenant credit, meaningful amortization and ratings that remain defensible under regulatory review.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally across the curve as oil's retreat eases inflation pressure
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied across the curve on Aug. 25. The 2-year yield fell 5.9 basis points to 4.175%, the 5-year dropped 6.6 basis points to 4.336%, the 10-year declined 6.8 basis points to 4.63% and the 30-year fell 6.1 basis points to 5.166%. The 10-year real yield accounted for most of the nominal move, while a 1.6-basis-point decline in the 10-year breakeven showed that inflation compensation also eased.

Brent fell 6.69% to $86 and WTI lost 4.65% to $81.06 as Iran and Oman discussed an interim framework to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and concern about renewed full-scale conflict receded. Shipping and insurance conditions had not normalized, but the scale of the oil decline provided a direct disinflationary impulse and brought policy-sensitive maturities more fully into the rally.

US data remained uneven. Consumer confidence fell to a 7-month low as expectations weakened, while present conditions, weekly employment growth and retail indicators were firmer. Susan Collins and Tom Barkin supported patience but kept further tightening conditional on sustained disinflation, making the front-end move a reduction in immediate policy pressure rather than a settled end to the debate.

Treasury buybacks continued to support long-end performance against swaps and encouraged bullish options positioning, but criticism from Stanley Druckenmiller and rising fiscal demands questioned whether debt management could durably lower borrowing costs. Risk assets advanced and volatility declined, while gold rose and the dollar softened slightly. AI financing also continued to expand across currencies and private structures, increasing scrutiny of funding capacity, creditor priority and insurer capital treatment.
